## Historical audit: S0027

**Scope:** Visible chunk 1 of 2 only. All citations refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_129095630/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The assigned goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching camera and framing. The student’s workshop interpretation is an inferred scene goal, not independent evidence of the reference’s contents. The reference image itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Student response and execute, lines 3–4 | The first program specified many objects: boards, a workbench and drawers, tools, cans, stool, neighboring furniture, and a carousel. It used procedural grain, roughness and metallic settings; placed separate parts by coordinates; and specified angled tools, a camera and two area lights. Those operations do not establish correct connections, pose, materials, occlusion or framing. |
| Execution result, line 5; student request, line 6 | Step 1 failed at `world.color` because the world was `None`; no image was returned. The runner supplied the traceback and requested a revised program. This is feedback actually received by the student, not teacher advice. |
| Student response and execute, lines 8–9; result, line 10 | The revision created a world if absent, assigned unique scene-member names and changed carousel dividers. Step 2 timed out after approximately 600 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and no image. The cause of the timeout is unestablished. |
| Student response and execute, lines 13–14; result, line 15 | The third program reduced geometric detail, replaced the cup’s many wall elements with one shell, used procedural surface variation, and reduced Cycles samples from 48 to 16 with denoising. Execution reported `ok: true`, a completed render and saved image and blend file (line 15, characters [0,132686)). This is technical validation, not visual or geometric verification. |
| Select event, line 16 | Step 3 was selected. This supports a successful build and selection, but not formal reconstruction correctness. |

**Input and autonomy.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible in this chunk. The student independently revised code in response to runner errors; the recorded sessions show no student tool calls (lines 2, 7 and 12). No rendered image was available for comparison before the third execution, and no subsequent visual review is visible here.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The visible history contains an execution error, a technical timeout, then a successful render and selection—not an empty patch. Overall visual success or partial correctness is unknown. Multiple modeled objects and intended part relationships are evidenced by code, but their actual connections, pose, appearance and correspondence to the reference remain unverified. Camera and lights were configured, yet any framing, lighting or render-quality issues remain unknown. Later events in the unseen chunk cannot be inferred.

**Lessons.** Transferable: distinguish execution success from scene fidelity, and use explicit runtime feedback when revising. The observed simplification preceded a successful run, but does not prove which change resolved the timeout. Task-specific choices—including workshop objects, grain and camera coordinates—remain hypotheses until compared visually with the reference.
